rationale: The core new logic gets genuine, would-fail-if-wrong tests: uiautomator2_backend_test.dart exercises the real _parseSource against a checked-in fixture (class->role mapping, bounds->rect, content-desc as label fallback and a11yId, resource-id-vs-positional xpath synthesis including a duplicate-resource-id edge case), the Android press vocabulary (back/enter succeed, consent_accept/alert_dismiss/unknown throw NativeException with a check that no /alert/accept request fired), and the enterText masked-flag derivation in both directions (password=true -> masked:true + attribute/text read + no attribute/value hit + back-key dismiss; password=false -> masked:false + exact readback). native_backend_factory_test.dart directly locks android->UiAutomator2Backend, ios->AppiumBackend, an unknown platform throwing ArgumentError (not silently defaulting to iOS), and the server override threading through — all positive and negative controls that would break if the switch in backendForPlatform regressed. Gaps: resolve() (the 4-tier a11yId/label/xpath/rect-center chain), tap(), swipe(), connect()/close() network behavior, and watch()/snapshot() are new code in uiautomator2_backend.dart with zero unit coverage in this diff — this mirrors the pre-existing AppiumBackend test's own gap (parity, not a regression introduced here) and is nominally caught by the hardware-gated live e2e, but that e2e self-skips in CI so these paths are asserted nowhere in the automated suite. More concretely, Step 4's new host-runner behavior — backendForPlatform's ArgumentError being caught and turned into stderr + exit(64) in bin/leonard_native_host.dart — is genuinely new control flow with no test anywhere (not even the existing iOS native_host_e2e_test.dart exercises a bad --platform value); the validation plan only greps for the call-site text, which proves the wiring exists but not that it behaves correctly at runtime. Net: main path (parsing, press, masking, platform selection) is meaningfully covered with real failure-mode assertions, but several new code paths (resolve/tap/swipe, and the host's new error-exit branch) are untested even nominally.
